selectivity.title: Selectivity Analysis
selectivity.tipEthrBody:
Resonant field at which capsid/cell-wall disruption triggers.
Disruption ratio = (E / E_thr) × L(f, f_res, Q) ≥ 1.0 → disruption
selectivity.tipNoGhzResBody:
Mammalian cells lack rigid-shell resonance, Schwan Vm → 0
at GHz (ωτ ≫ 1). Healthy tissue is unperturbed.
selectivity.tipVmSarResonance: Disruption & Thermal, Resonance Mode T-Disr: capsid disruption % = (E/E_thr) × L(f,f_res,Q) H-Safe: healthy Vm → 0 at GHz, unperturbed SAR = σ_i·α²·E²·wf / ρ, valid in all modes Use duty cycle to limit thermal load.
selectivity.tipVmSarSchwan: Transmembrane Potential & SAR Vm = 1.5·E·R / √(1+(ωτ)²) τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i)/(2σ_e·σ_i) SAR = σ_i·α²·E²·wf / ρ α = 3σ_e/(2σ_e+σ_i), internal field factor wf = 0.5 (CW) or 1.0 (pulsed)
selectivity.tipTargetLysisField: Target Lysis Field Minimum E to reach lysis threshold at current frequency. E_lysis = Vm_thr · √(1+(ωτ)²) / (1.5·R)
selectivity.tipHealthyLysisField: Healthy Lysis Field Minimum E to reach lysis threshold at current frequency. Keep operating field below this for selective therapy.
selectivity.tipSkinDepth: EM Skin Depth δ δ = √(1/(π·f·μ₀·σ_e)) Field decays to 1/e (~37%) in saline (σ_e = 1.5 S/m). 100 MHz → 41 mm · 1 GHz → 13 mm · 12 GHz → 3.8 mm ≥20 mm: tissue-penetrating 5-20 mm: cm-depth accessible <5 mm: near-surface / intracavitary applicator needed Ref: Gabriel et al. (1996) Phys. Med. Biol. 41:2271
selectivity.tipFresRange: f_res Uncertainty Range f_res = v_sound / (2R), uncertainty from v_sound range. Bacteria: v_wall ≈ 800-1200 m/s → ±25-30% Enveloped viruses: v_eff poorly defined → ±40% Tune frequency experimentally within this range.
selectivity.tipQFactor: Q-Factor Uncertainty Q sets the resonance linewidth. Lower Q → broader resonance, weaker peak amplitude. Dykeman & Sankey (2010) validated Q on rigid icosahedral capsids only. Bacterial peptidoglycan and viral lipid envelopes have substantially lower Q.
selectivity.tipBasis: Experimental Basis LASER-VALIDATED: confirmed by pulsed laser (Tsen 2007-2012) RF-EXTRAPOLATED: acoustic mechanism plausible; GHz RF delivery not yet validated experimentally SPECULATIVE: no experimental validation by any method Ref: Tsen et al. (2007); Dykeman & Sankey (2010)
selectivity.tipModeBadge: Therapeutic Mode Therapeutic DR_T >85%, DR_H <50% Target at lysis threshold · healthy safely below 50% Marginal DR_T >85%, DR_H 50-84% Healthy cells stressed, adjust field or frequency Approaching DR_T 50-85% Increase field to reach therapeutic window Sub-threshold DR_T <50%, field too low Ablative DR_H >85% Non-selective, both cell types at lysis

selectivity.tipOrientFrac: Random-Orientation Lysis Probability In a real experiment cells are randomly oriented. The Schwan Vm has a cosθ factor: Vm(θ) = 1.5·E·R·cosθ / √(1+(ωτ)²) For a 3D isotropic distribution, the fraction of cells with Vm > V_thr is: P = max(0, 1 − 1/DR) where DR = Vm_max / V_thr Examples: DR = 1.0 → 0% of cells lyse (none aligned enough) DR = 2.0 → 50% lyse DR = 5.0 → 80% lyse Resonance mode (bacteria/virus): acoustic pressure is nearly omnidirectional , the cosθ formula does not apply. Orientation fraction shows, in that mode.
selectivity.tipDep: Dielectrophoresis (DEP) Clausius-Mossotti factor K(ω), single-shell sphere model. K(ω) = (ε*_eff − ε*_m) / (ε*_eff + 2ε*_m) ε*(ω) = ε_r·ε₀ − jσ/ω pDEP Re[K] > 0, cell attracted to field maxima nDEP Re[K] < 0, cell repelled from field maxima f_cross, crossover frequency where Re[K] = 0 Effective time-averaged force scales: CW sinusoidal: × 0.50 Pulsed H-FIRE: × duty cycle Ref: Gascoyne & Vykoukal (2002) Curr. Opin. Cell Biol. Note: model invalid at GHz acoustic resonance frequencies.
